items.entity: design domain Ω of the Fig. 1 example
items.description: Sec. 2 says only 'An open domain ... is to be designed on'; the shape, aspect ratio and size of the Fig. 1 domain are visible only in the figure. Sec. 5.1 uses a 64×64 square domain for the dataset, but Fig. 1 is not stated to be a dataset sample.
readings: Square domain, aspect ratio 1:1 (matches the 64×64 dataset domain)
Irregular schematic domain Ω placed inside a rectangular grid, with void passive elements outside Ω

items.entity: finite-element discretization (number and type of elements)
items.description: Sec. 2 only says the domain is discretized into elements; no element count or type is given for Fig. 1. The 64×64 grid of square elements is stated only for the dataset (Sec. 5.1).
readings: 64 elements on the short side with a proportional long side (e.g., 128×64 for a 2:1 domain)

items.description: Where ∂Ω_D lies, how long it is, and how many supports there are are shown only in Fig. 1 (caption: 'specific combination of boundary condition ∂Ω_D and load P'). The dataset (Sec. 5.1, Fig. 4) uses 1–4 of 16 options: 4 corner points, 4 mid-side points, and 8 half-edges between them.
readings: One corner point plus one mid-side point (e.g., (0,0) and (0,0.5H))

items.entity: point of application of force P
items.description: The point where P is applied appears only in Fig. 1. Sec. 2 gives no location, and Sec. 5.1 only says a random boundary element is used for dataset samples.
readings: Mid-span of the top or bottom edge (x=0.5L)

items.description: The direction of P is shown only by the arrow in Fig. 1. The dataset rule in Sec. 5.1 ('from 0 to 2π, sampled from 6 evenly distributed values') is itself ambiguous (multiples of 60°, or 72° steps if both 0 and 2π are included), and the reference axis and sense of the angle are not given.
readings: Inclined at 72°, 144°, 216° or 288° from +x (6 values including both 0 and 2π)

items.description: |P| is not given in Sec. 2 or in the Fig. 1 caption; dataset loads have unit magnitude (Sec. 5.1).

items.entity: how force P is applied (node vs. element)
items.description: Sec. 2 shows P as a single force vector, but Sec. 5.1 says a boundary 'element' is chosen as the load location. Whether the force goes on one node or is spread over the element's nodes is not stated.
readings: Point force on a single boundary node
Force split equally between the two boundary nodes of the loaded element edge (uniform traction over one element)
Force split equally among the 4 nodes of the selected boundary element

items.description: Sec. 2 says only 'some volume fraction f'; no value is given for the Fig. 1 example (dataset targets are 30–50%, Sec. 5.1).
Eq. (4) is written in terms of the design variables x, but the structure is defined by the filtered densities x̃ (Eq. 7). The text does not say which one the constraint uses.
readings: Constraint on the filtered physical densities x̃
Constraint on the raw design variables x (literal Eq. 4)

items.description: Sec. 2 defines E0 only as a symbol; a unit modulus is stated only for the dataset FE fields (Sec. 5.1).
Not mentioned in Sec. 2. Sec. 5.1 gives ν = 0.3 'for the calculation of the finite element fields' of the dataset, not explicitly for the Fig. 1 optimization.
Sec. 2 gives Emin only approximately: 'a small stiffness (~0.001E0)'.
readings: Emin = 1e-9·E0 (common SIMP default, if '~' is read loosely)

items.description: Sec. 2 introduces p without a value. Sec. 5.1 gives 'a penalty parameter of 3' for the dataset; it does not say whether Fig. 1 uses it or whether p is ramped up (continuation).
r_min in Eq. (6) has no value in Sec. 2. Sec. 5.1 gives 'a density filter radius of 2.0' with no units (element widths vs. length) and only for the 64×64 dataset.
readings: r_min = 2/64 of the domain side (≈0.031·L), converted to elements if the Fig. 1 mesh is not 64×64
r_min = 1.5 element widths (common default, if Fig. 1 is not a dataset run)

items.entity: density-filter weight w_ei and neighbourhood N_e (Eq. 6)
items.description: Eq. (6) w_ei = r_min − |x_i − x_e| uses the density symbols x_i, x_e (as in Eqs. 1, 5, 7), which makes it a density-difference weight. The text, however, describes spatial blurring of neighbours, which needs a distance-based weight. N_e and a max(0,·) cut-off are not defined.
readings: Standard linear hat filter: w_ei = max(0, r_min − ‖c_i − c_e‖) using element-centre distances, with N_e = {i : ‖c_i − c_e‖ < r_min}
Literal density-difference weight r_min − |x_i − x_e|, applied over the spatial neighbourhood within r_min

items.description: Sec. 2: densities are 'updated using the gradient of the compliance, propagated back'; Sec. 5.1: 'a gradient descent algorithm'. The update rule, step size or move limit, and how the volume constraint is enforced are not given.
readings: Optimality Criteria (move limit 0.2, damping 0.5, bisection on the Lagrange multiplier)
Projected (clamped to [0,1]) gradient descent or an autograd optimizer, with volume enforced by Lagrange-multiplier bisection or a penalty

items.description: The starting density field is not stated (Sec. 5.1 only mentions an 'initial unoptimized domain').
Sec. 2 iterates 'until convergence is reached' with no tolerance or iteration cap.
Plane stress vs. plane strain and the out-of-plane thickness are not stated (thickness only scales compliance; plane strain changes the effective ν).
Sec. 2 calls compliance 'the total strain energy', but Eq. (2) defines c = UᵀKU, which is twice the strain energy.
Neither Sec. 2 nor the Fig. 1 caption mentions passive solid or void regions. 'Open domain' suggests there are none, but the figure cannot be checked.
readings: Solid passive elements around the load point and/or supports
Void passive elements outside a non-rectangular Ω
